newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police search Salinas ranch for corpse.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police search Salinas ranch for corpse.

text.p: Police using a bulldozer on Tuesday searched a ranch belonging to the jailed brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas amid reports of a possible breakthrough in the case of a major political assassination.

Raul Salinas's lawyer said police were searching for the corpse of Manuel Munoz Rocha, who, alongside Raul, is an alleged mastermind of the murder in September 1994 of ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) leader Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
Raul Salinas is currently in jail and Munoz Rocha has been missing since shortly after the killing, presumed dead.
But the Salinas lawyer, Raul Gonzalez Salas, said no body had been found and the search had been postponed until Wednesday morning because of bad weather.
"There is a warrant to search the property with the aim of seeking the supposed corpse of Manuel Munoz Rocha," Gonzalez Salas said on national television network TV Azteca.
"They have brought in a bulldozer to carry out deep excavations, they've been working since the afternoon and absolutely nothing has turned up," he said.

A Reuters photographer at the scene, in the capital's western suburb of Cuajimalpa, said some 60 armed police, along with the bulldozer, were searching the ranch in the dark. At the site was Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, a special prosecutor in charge of the Ruiz Massieu murder investigation.
TV Azteca said Chapa was accompanied by two clairvoyants who have helped in the search for Munoz Rocha.
The attorney general's office confirmed there was a police operation at the site, but declined to give further details.
